claims.text: Adding approximately 0.1 at.% boron to CrFeNiTi-based solid-solution nanoparticles induces nanoscale boride precipitation at internal interfaces or grain boundaries.
Interfacial boride precipitates act as pinning centers that retard grain-boundary motion and grain growth.
Interfacial boride precipitates retard atomic diffusion.
Boron-induced borides preserve the structural and chemical stability of CrFeNiTi-based nanoparticles under catalytic and thermoelectric service temperatures.
Undoped CrFeNiTi-based nanoparticles typically have high grain-boundary mobility.
Undoped CrFeNiTi-based nanoparticles are prone to high-temperature coarsening.
Undoped CrFeNiTi-based nanoparticles are prone to high-temperature chemical segregation.
Incorporating approximately 0.1 at.% boron during synthesis promotes boron segregation and intergranular boride formation.
During rapid solidification, boron preferentially segregates to nanoparticle interfaces.
The segregated boron precipitates as stable borides resembling (Hf,Zr)B2.
Boron-doped nanoparticles will coarsen less than undoped nanoparticles during high-temperature exposure.
Boron-doped nanoparticles will undergo slower elemental segregation than undoped nanoparticles.
Boron-doped nanoparticles will retain catalytic activity better than undoped nanoparticles after repeated high-temperature exposure.
Boron-doped nanoparticles will retain thermoelectric performance better than undoped nanoparticles after repeated high-temperature exposure.
The proposed mechanism applies to CrFeNiTi-based solid-solution nanoparticles at approximately 0.1 at.% boron.
Excessive boron can form continuous brittle phases.
Bulk-alloy evidence shows that 0.1 at.% boron can induce intergranular borides and improve grain-boundary cohesion.
The precipitation kinetics and grain-boundary behavior of boron-containing nanoparticles may differ from those of bulk alloys.
A lack of statistically significant improvement in grain growth, segregation, and performance degradation relative to an undoped control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The target material is stated to be CrFeNiTi-based, but the proposed precipitate is exemplified as an (Hf,Zr)B2-like phase even though Hf and Zr are not included in the stated target composition. The cited (Hf,Zr)B2 observation comes from a different HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy.
